conflicting_existing_evidence.source: Rayls Testnet Explorer transaction logs endpoint

assessment.finding: The RPC eth_getLogs scan returned zero Upgraded events over a range that includes the proxy creation block, even though Explorer reports an Upgraded(address) event in the creation transaction at that block.
assessment.conclusion: The zero-event RPC scan is not a complete or reconcilable historical log record. It cannot be used to infer that no upgrades occurred between deployment and the target transaction.
possible_explanations_not_yet_tested: Historical log indexing or retention gap for old blocks in the RPC endpoint.
A difference between the RPC log backend and Explorer indexed logs.
An endpoint-specific query/index issue for the creation block.
explicitly_not_concluded: No upgrade occurred between deployment and 2026-11-21.
Implementation 0x0a3a... remained active until the target transaction.
The exact root cause of the RPC-versus-Explorer log discrepancy.

next_checks: Query /api/v2/addresses/{proxy}/transactions and inspect its items and next_page_params to establish whether the address-level transaction index is usable.

If address transactions are indexed, page through proxy interactions from creation to block 24825928 and inspect calldata selectors for UUPS upgrade calls (including upgradeTo(address) and upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes)) and other admin actions.
Fetch transaction-specific logs/receipts for any candidate upgrade transactions to verify the Upgraded(address) event and new implementation address.
If address transactions also omit known creation or upgrade records, use Explorer's block transaction listing or an independent archive data source instead.
Do not infer that implementation 0x0a3a... remained active at the target transaction until a complete upgrade timeline or historical slot proof is obtained.

scan_exact_block_controls.retrieval_method: eth_getLogs with exact fromBlock and toBlock

results.filter: proxy address only, without topic filter

scan_exact_block_controls.assessment: The RPC endpoint returns no logs for the exact proxy creation block even without a topic filter, while it returns the two known later upgrade logs at their exact blocks. This localizes the discrepancy to historical log availability/indexing for the creation block or older data, but does not establish the precise cause or prove no intermediate upgrades.

explorer_v2_address_logs_check.comparison: The endpoint returned no items and no pagination cursor, while the Explorer transaction-specific endpoint for the proxy creation transaction returned an Upgraded(address) event at creation block 21568375.
explorer_v2_address_logs_check.conclusion: The address-level logs endpoint cannot be used to reconstruct the pre-transaction upgrade history from its returned first page. This does not establish that no proxy logs or upgrades occurred.
explorer_v2_address_logs_check.note: The documented Blockscout v2 endpoint shape includes items and next_page_params. In this Rayls response both were empty/null.
